post.post_content:
The best cloud hosting is the one that matches how much of the server you want to manage. Cloudways is the best managed cloud for most sites, Kinsta is the best premium choice for WordPress, and DigitalOcean is the best unmanaged option for developers. This page compares 7 cloud hosts on price, renewals and what you manage yourself. We read each host's own pages between 15 and 18 November 2026, and we researched independent test reports for every host.

What is cloud hosting?

Cloud hosting runs your site on a network of connected servers instead of one machine. HostingAdvice says this improves reliability, uptime and flexibility compared with shared or VPS hosting. In practice, you buy a set amount of CPU and memory on that network, and many hosts let you add more when traffic grows.

Cloud hosting, shared hosting and VPS: what changes?

TypeWho shares the resourcesEntry price on our listsGrowing the plan
SharedMany sites share one serverFrom $1.99 a month (Hostinger Premium)Move up a plan, with limits
VPSA fixed slice of one server is yoursFrom $59 a month for a managed VPS (Liquid Web)Move to a bigger slice
CloudA dedicated slice on a network of serversFrom $4 a month (DigitalOcean) to $100 (SiteGround Cloud)Add resources, or autoscale on some plans

A small site does not need cloud hosting. Finding the Universe suggests shared hosting for sites under about 10,000 visitors a month and a VPS or cloud plan from there.

How much does cloud hosting cost?

Prices below are what each host lists on its own page. The twelve-month figures are our own arithmetic at the standard monthly price, so check the renewal before you buy.

HostEntry planStandard monthly priceTwelve months at that pricePrice rises?
DigitalOcean1 GiB Droplet$6$72 (backups add 20% to 30%)No
CloudwaysFlexible entry (DigitalOcean)$11$132No
Hostinger Cloud Startup48-month term$25.99 after the term$311.88Yes, from $7.99
KinstaBusiness Single 20GB$35$420No
ScalaHosting Entry Cloud2 cores, 2 GB RAM$39.95$479.40Yes, from $11.21 (Black Friday)
Liquid WebManaged VPS$59$708Sale only
SiteGround CloudJump Start$100$1,200No

Hosting Ranked puts entry-level unmanaged cloud at about $4 to $6 a month, managed cloud at $14 to $28 and premium managed cloud at $35 to $115. The hosts above fit those bands.

Managed or unmanaged cloud hosting?

Managed means the host updates the server, sets up caching and watches security. Cloudways, Kinsta, ScalaHosting, SiteGround Cloud and Liquid Web do this to different degrees. Unmanaged means you do it. DigitalOcean is the clearest example: the price is low, and the server is yours to look after.

Is cloud hosting faster and safer than shared hosting?

Not by itself. A cloud plan with enough CPU and memory holds up better under load, which is why several tests above use many concurrent users. But a slow site stays slow without caching. On a $6 DigitalOcean Droplet, a page cache cut first-byte time from 1.66 seconds to 0.40 seconds. On safety, managed hosts add firewalls, patching and backups. SiteGround Cloud lists a firewall with WordPress rules, and Kinsta lists daily backups. On an unmanaged server you add these yourself.

How does uptime compare?

HostUptime in the tests we readSource
Kinsta100% on 20 monitored sitesWP Umbrella
ScalaHosting100% in four independent testsFour test reports
Cloudways99.996% to 99.999% across five plansHostingstep
Hostinger Cloud StartupNo downtime in 30 days on one test serverHostingGuider

These are short windows, so treat them as a snapshot, not a promise. A host's own uptime guarantee is a separate thing, and the credit for missing it is usually small.

Which cloud host fits which job?

If you areLook atWhy
A beginner who wants a dashboardCloudways or Hostinger Cloud StartupThe host manages the server and the price is clear
An agency with client sitesSiteGround Cloud or KinstaSiteGround lets you build your own plans and client roles
Running an online storeLiquid Web, Kinsta or CloudwaysLiquid Web held 1,000 concurrent users with 0% errors in two tests
Expecting traffic spikesSiteGround Cloud or CloudwaysSiteGround offers autoscaling and Cloudways has an autoscaling plan
A developer who wants the lowest priceDigitalOceanDroplets start at $4 a month and you control the server

How do you move a site to cloud hosting?

  • Back up the site and the database before you start.
  • Choose a server region near your visitors.
  • Copy the files and database, or use the host's free migration. Kinsta, Liquid Web and Hostinger list free migration, and SiteGround lists a migrator plugin.
  • Test the new site on a temporary address and check every form and checkout.
  • Lower the domain's TTL a day ahead, then switch the domain and watch for errors.

A move that changes URLs or loses redirects can cost rankings. If you want the move done and checked for you, see our website maintenance services.

How did we choose these hosts?

  • We read each host's own site. Plans, prices and terms come from the company pages.
  • We used named tests. Every speed and uptime figure comes from a published test with its method and date.
  • We compared the top-ranking guides. We read what the best cloud hosting pages cover and answered the questions they cover.
  • We show the renewal price. A low sale price is not a bargain if it rises 3 times after the term.

What should you check before you buy cloud hosting?

  • CPU cores and memory. These set how many pages the server can build at the same time. HostingGuider compares plans by cores and RAM for this reason.
  • The term and renewal price. Write both down before you pay.
  • Where the server is. HostingGuider's Singapore server answered in 157 ms from Singapore and 674 ms from Sydney. Choose a region near your visitors.
  • Backups. Check how many days are kept and whether they cost extra.
  • Who you can reach. Kinsta and SiteGround Cloud list human support. DigitalOcean charges for chat.
  • Card payments. Hostinger is not PCI compliant. Check how your payment provider handles it.

For all-round picks that include shared hosting, read our best web hosting services guide.

rl_answer: The best cloud hosting depends on how much of the server you want to manage. Cloudways is the best managed cloud for most sites, Kinsta is the best premium choice for WordPress, and DigitalOcean is the best unmanaged option for developers.
rl_faqs:
What is cloud hosting? | Cloud hosting runs your site on a network of connected servers, not one machine. HostingAdvice says this improves reliability, uptime and flexibility compared with shared or VPS hosting.
How is cloud hosting different from shared hosting and VPS? | Shared hosting puts many sites on one server and they share its resources. A VPS gives you a fixed slice of one server. Cloud hosting gives you a slice on a network of servers, and many hosts let you add resources quickly.
How much does cloud hosting cost? | On this list a cloud plan runs from $4 a month (DigitalOcean) to $100 a month (SiteGround Cloud). Cloudways starts at $11 and Kinsta at $35. Hosting Ranked puts entry-level unmanaged cloud at about $4 to $6, managed cloud at $14 to $28 and premium managed cloud at $35 to $115.
Is cloud hosting good for WordPress? | Yes. Cloudways, Kinsta, ScalaHosting, SiteGround Cloud and Liquid Web all run WordPress well. Kinsta and SiteGround Cloud are built for it. DigitalOcean is fast, but it needs a page cache to be quick on WordPress.
Should I choose managed or unmanaged cloud hosting? | Choose managed if you do not want to patch servers, set up caching and watch security yourself. Choose unmanaged, such as a DigitalOcean Droplet, if you can run a server and want the lowest price.
Which cloud host is the fastest? | It depends on the test and the location. Webhostingcat measured a 77 ms time to first byte on Kinsta, and HostingGuider measured 157 ms on a Hostinger Cloud Startup server in Singapore. Test methods differ, so compare each number with its method.
Do I need AWS or Google Cloud directly? | Most sites do not. AWS and Google Cloud give you the most control, but the pricing is complex and you set everything up. Cloudways and Kinsta put a managed layer on top of them.
Does the renewal price matter for cloud hosting? | Yes for fixed-term plans. Hostinger Cloud Startup renews at 3.3 times its sale price and ScalaHosting Entry Cloud at 3.6 times. Cloudways and DigitalOcean charge the same price every month.
Does cloud hosting handle traffic spikes? | Some plans do. SiteGround Cloud offers autoscaling, and Cloudways has an autoscaling WordPress plan. On a fixed plan, a spike beyond your CPU and RAM still slows the site, so check the limits.
Where should the server be? | Close to your visitors. In HostingGuider's test a Singapore server answered in 157 ms from Singapore and 674 ms from Sydney.
Can I host more than one website on cloud hosting? | Often yes. SiteGround Cloud lists unlimited websites and Hostinger Cloud Startup lists unlimited sites. Kinsta limits sites by plan, so check the plan page.
Do I need technical skills to use cloud hosting? | Not on a managed plan. Cloudways, Kinsta and ScalaHosting give you a dashboard and handle the server. On DigitalOcean you need to be comfortable with servers.
How do I move my site to cloud hosting? | Back up the site, choose a server region near your visitors, copy the files and database, test on a temporary address, then switch the domain. Kinsta, Liquid Web and Hostinger list free migration, and SiteGround lists a free migrator plugin.
Is cloud hosting good for an online store? | It can be. Liquid Web handled 1,000 concurrent users with 0% errors in two tests, though one test saw a slow WooCommerce checkout. Kinsta and Cloudways are common choices for stores.
Which cloud host is best for agencies? | SiteGround Cloud lets you build your own plans and give clients their own roles. Kinsta and Cloudways are also popular with agencies.
Which cloud host has the best uptime? | In the tests we read, Kinsta recorded 100% on 20 monitored sites, ScalaHosting 100% in four tests and Cloudways 99.996% to 99.999% across five plans. Test windows are short, so treat uptime as a snapshot.
